account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led registration clinical trial for China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). cnBeta and Kuai Keji reported the operation on 12 March 2022, and both cited the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. The reports describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. The reports say that the device predicts an imminent seizure and delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. They call bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly, and the stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement and clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The initial accounts give no seizure outcome, patient age or follow-up for this patient. In 2023 the Xuanwu Hospital team and two partner centers reported that 10 patients were enrolled in the first-in-human trial between March and November 2022. They reported that seven patients followed over three months had a mean seizure reduction of 61.1%, with no serious adverse events. A later eight-center report by the same group describes 19 patients through June 2023, with a median reduction of 58% at month 12 and seizure-free periods in four patients. That paper identifies the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech. It describes five clinician-configured detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. It does not establish that a learned model predicted seizures. Neither paper gives the first patient's own outcome. The 2022 news reports relay the hospital's WeChat post.

fields.account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led registration clinical trial for China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). cnBeta and Kuai Keji reported the operation on 12 March 2022, and both cited the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. The reports describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. The reports say that the device predicts an imminent seizure and delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. They call bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly, and the stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement and clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The initial accounts give no seizure outcome, patient age or follow-up for this patient. In 2023 the Xuanwu Hospital team and two partner centers reported that 10 patients were enrolled in the first-in-human trial between March and November 2022. They reported that seven patients followed over three months had a mean seizure reduction of 61.1%, with no serious adverse events. A later eight-center report by the same group describes 19 patients through June 2023, with a median reduction of 58% at month 12 and seizure-free periods in four patients. That paper identifies the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech. It describes five clinician-configured detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. It does not establish that a learned model predicted seizures. Neither paper gives the first patient's own outcome. The 2022 news reports relay the hospital's WeChat post.
fields.summary: Xuanwu Hospital implanted the Epilcure responsive neurostimulator in a man with epilepsy in March 2022; its trial team reports a 61.1% mean seizure reduction in seven patients and no result for him.
